name: p_sshi_full_bridge
rationale: The reference FBR fails because the open-circuit voltage (3.8V) is too low to overcome diode drops and reach the 4.5V target. P-SSHI (Parallel Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor) uses an LC resonance to invert the voltage across the piezo capacitance Cp at its extrema. This effectively boosts the voltage available to the rectifier, allowing the output to reach the target range. I use a full-bridge rectifier with low-drop Schottky diodes (DSCH) to maximize efficiency.

name: p_sshi_half_bridge
rationale: Similar to the full-bridge P-SSHI, but uses a half-bridge rectifier configuration to reduce the number of diodes in the conduction path from two to one. By placing a large bias capacitor from pzn to ground, the circuit can extract energy during one half-cycle with lower voltage drop, potentially improving startup time and minimum output voltage under light excitation.

name: p_sshi_half_bridge_pos
rationale: The previous half-bridge SSHI (edges=both) harvested too much power, causing Vout to exceed 5.5V and the output to drift (fail settled) as it slowly climbed towards a high equilibrium. By changing to edges=pos, we halve the energy harvested per cycle. This should lower Vavg and Vmax to the target 4.5-5.5V range and allow the output to settle faster. I also increase C1 to 22uF to significantly reduce the ripple Vpp, while accepting that the reduced power will balance the settling time.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_pos
rationale: Similar to the half-bridge pos, this uses a full-bridge rectifier but limits the flipping to one peak per cycle (edges=pos). This combines the efficiency of the full-bridge for low-excitation cases (S4) with a power reduction mechanism to prevent overvoltage on S1-S3. A larger C1 is used to stabilize the output and meet ripple requirements.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_clamped
rationale: The full-bridge SSHI delivers sufficient power to meet vout_min across all conditions, but it suffers from excessive output voltage (vmax) and ripple, especially under strong excitation or light loads (S3). To regulate the output within the 4.5V to 5.5V window, I am adding a shunt regulator. By placing three DSI diodes (each ~0.5V drop) and one DZ33 Zener (3.3V breakdown) in series from the output node to ground, the combined breakdown voltage is approximately 4.8V. This will clamp the output voltage effectively, preventing overvoltage while ensuring the minimum supply of 4.5V is maintained for all cases.

name: p_sshi_half_bridge_biased
rationale: The previous full-bridge SSHI was close to the target but failed on underpower (S2, S4, S6) due to the two-diode drop in the rectification path. A half-bridge SSHI reduces this to a single-diode drop. By adding a bias diode (D2) from the output back to the piezo's negative terminal (pzn), the piezo is effectively biased at Vout, allowing D1 to conduct whenever Vpzp exceeds Vout. This significantly increases the energy delivered to the storage capacitor and should lift vavg above 4.5V for all conditions.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_clamp4
rationale: The full-bridge SSHI is highly efficient, which causes vout to exceed 5.5 V on several conditions (up to 15.3 V on S3). To limit the voltage while maintaining it above 4.5 V, I am adding a shunt clamp consisting of one DZ33 Zener and four DSI silicon diodes in series. This creates a conduction path from 'out' to ground when Vout exceeds approximately 3.3 + 4*0.5 = 5.3 V. I also increased C1 to 10 uF to mitigate the ripple issue seen in the best previous design.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_clamp3
rationale: Similar to the previous proposal, but using three DSI diodes in the clamp. This reduces the clamp voltage to approximately 3.3 + 3*0.5 = 4.8 V. This provides a tighter ceiling, ensuring vout_max <= 5.5 V while still allowing the output to settle comfortably above the 4.5 V minimum.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_silicon
rationale: Replacing the low-drop DSCH Schottky diodes with higher-drop DSI silicon diodes in the rectifier bridge. This increases the series voltage drop by 0.5 V, which may help in reducing vout_max on nominally strong conditions without needing a shunt clamp, while still utilizing the SSHI boost to reach 4.5 V.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_zener_clamp
rationale: The previous best design 'p_sshi_full_bridge' delivered sufficient power to meet vout_min and startup requirements but failed vout_max because the output was unregulated. I am adding a voltage clamp consisting of a Zener diode (DZ33) and a chain of four silicon diodes (DSI) to limit the output voltage to approximately 5.3V (3.3V + 4 * 0.5V). The Zener cathode is connected to the 'out' node to ensure conduction only when the voltage exceeds the threshold. This should satisfy vout_max while maintaining the power delivery of the full-bridge SSHI topology.

name: p_sshi_full_bridge_filtered_clamp
rationale: The previous best design (c0143) failed only on S3 ripple (60mV vs 50mV limit). S3 is the strong excitation case, which delivers larger charge pulses. To reduce ripple without simply increasing the storage capacitor C1 (which would slow down the S4 startup), I am adding a filter inductor L2 between the rectifier output and the storage node 'out'. This creates an LC filter that smooths the charging current spikes, reducing output ripple while maintaining the fast startup and precise clamping voltage of the existing design.

name: p_sshi_pi_filter_clamp
rationale: The previous best design failed only on S3 ripple (60mV vs 50mV limit). The current LC filter is not sufficiently suppressing the charging spikes from the SSHI rectifier. By adding a pre-filter capacitor (C_pre) at the rectifier output, we create a Pi-filter (C-L-C), which provides much better ripple suppression for the same total capacitance, thus maintaining fast startup (tup) and stability (dv) while meeting the strict ripple requirement on S3.

name: p_sshi_double_l_filter_clamp
rationale: The previous L-C filter design was very close, failing only on S3 ripple (60mV vs 50mV limit). A second-order inductor filter (L2 and L3 in series) provides better high-frequency attenuation than a single inductor, which should push the ripple below 50mV. Since S4 startup has some margin in the L-C design, this approach is more likely to succeed than the pi-filter (which added too much capacitance and slowed startup).

name: p_sshi_lcl_filter_clamp
rationale: The previous best designs failed due to ripple on S3 (strong excitation) or slow startup on S4 (weak excitation). A Pi filter (C-L-C) reduced ripple but slowed startup. I am proposing an L-C-L filter (two inductors and two capacitors) which typically provides superior ripple attenuation for the same total capacitance, potentially satisfying both the ripple and startup constraints. Additionally, I have replaced the ineffective clamp from previous iterations with a genuine Zener-diode chain (3 x DSI + 1 x DZ33) connected from ground to 'out' to strictly limit vmax to ~5.1V.
